title: Off-by-one in range sum
description: Sums every integer from 1 up to and including n.
bugExplanation: range(1, n) stops at n-1, so n is never added. Use range(1, n + 1) to include n.
hints: The result is smaller than expected.
Check the upper bound of range().

title: Wrong remainder check
description: Returns True when a number is even.
bugExplanation: The function tests for a remainder of 1, which identifies odd numbers. Even numbers have remainder 0: n % 2 == 0.
hints: Look at what the modulo result means.

title: Missing return in helper
description: Computes the square of a number and uses it to sum squares.
bugExplanation: square() computes a value but never returns it, so it yields None and the addition raises TypeError. Add return result.

title: None used as counter
description: Counts how many vowels appear in a string.
bugExplanation: count starts as None, and None + 1 raises TypeError. Initialize the counter with 0.
hints: Inspect the initial value of count.

title: Wrong index for last element
description: Returns the final element of a non-empty list.
bugExplanation: Valid indexes run from 0 to len-1, so items[len(items)] raises IndexError. Use items[len(items) - 1] (or items[-1]).
hints: The last valid index is len - 1.

title: Infinite while loop
description: Builds a countdown list from n down to 1.
bugExplanation: The loop variable n is never changed so n > 0 stays True forever. Add n -= 1 in the loop body.
hints: Does the loop condition ever change?

title: Wrong comparison in max
description: Finds the largest number in a list.
bugExplanation: Using < keeps the smallest value instead of the largest. The condition must be n > best.
hints: Use greater-than to track a maximum.

title: String plus int concatenation
description: Builds a greeting that includes a name and age.
code:
def describe(name, age):
    msg = "Name: " + name + ", age: " + age
    return msg

print(describe("Ana", 30))
# Run the example above and compare the output with what is expected.
bugExplanation: Python cannot concatenate str and int. Convert age with str(age).
hints: A TypeError mentions str and int.
Convert the number to a string.

title: Wrong slice bound
description: Returns the first three items of a list.
bugExplanation: The slice [:2] gives two items. To get three items use items[:3].

title: Integer division in average
description: Computes the arithmetic mean of a list of numbers.
bugExplanation: // performs floor division and drops the fractional part. Use / for true division.

title: Wrong boolean operator in range
description: Checks whether x lies between lo and hi inclusive.
code:
def in_range(x, lo, hi):
    return x >= lo or x <= hi

print(in_range(5, 1, 10))
print(in_range(50, 1, 10))  # should be False
# Run the example above and compare the output with what is expected.
bugExplanation: With or, almost every number satisfies at least one side. Both bounds must hold, so use and.
hints: Consider which operator requires both conditions.

title: Wrong step in reverse slice
description: Checks whether a string reads the same backwards.
code:
def is_palindrome(s):
    s = s.lower()
    return s == s[::1]

print(is_palindrome("Level"))
print(is_palindrome("hello"))
bugExplanation: s[::1] copies the string unchanged, so the check is always True. Reverse with s[::-1].
hints: Everything is reported as a palindrome.
What does the slice step do?

title: KeyError on first word
description: Counts the occurrences of each word.
bugExplanation: Reading counts[w] for a new word raises KeyError. Use counts.get(w, 0) + 1.
hints: The key does not exist yet.

title: Wrong final return value
description: Returns True only when all numbers are positive.
bugExplanation: If no bad value is found the function should return True, but it returns False. Change the final return to True.
hints: What happens when the loop completes?

title: Mutable default argument
description: Adds an item to a bucket list and returns it.
code:
def add_item(item, bucket=[]):
    bucket.append(item)
    return bucket

print(add_item(1))
print(add_item(2))  # expected [2]
bugExplanation: The default list is created once and shared across calls. Use bucket=None and create a new list inside.

title: Removing while iterating
description: Removes all even numbers from a list in place.
bugExplanation: Removing items from a list while iterating skips elements. Iterate over a copy: for n in nums[:].

title: Late-binding lambda
description: Creates three functions returning 0, 1, 2.
code:
funcs = []
for i in range(3):
    funcs.append(lambda: i)

print([f() for f in funcs])  # expected [0, 1, 2]
# Run the example above and compare the output with what is expected.
bugExplanation: Lambdas capture the variable i, not its value, so all return 2. Bind the current value: lambda i=i: i.
hints: All lambdas return the same value.

title: Shared rows in grid
description: Creates a 3x3 grid of zeros.
code:
grid = [[0] * 3] * 3
grid[0][0] = 1
print(grid)  # expected only the first cell to change
for row in grid:
    print(row)
# Run the example above and compare the output with what is expected.
bugExplanation: Multiplying the outer list repeats references to the same inner list. Use [[0]*3 for _ in range(3)].
hints: The rows are the same object.

title: Binary search stuck
description: Returns the index of target in a sorted list or -1.
bugExplanation: Setting lo = mid can loop forever when lo == mid. Use lo = mid + 1.
hints: Does the range shrink each time?

title: Identity vs equality for strings
description: Prints a message when status is 'ok'.
bugExplanation: 'is' compares object identity, not value; strings built at runtime may be different objects. Use ==.

title: Global counter without declaration
description: Increments a module-level counter.
code:
counter = 0

def increment():
    counter += 1
    return counter

print(increment())
bugExplanation: Assigning to counter inside the function makes it local, raising UnboundLocalError. Declare global counter first.

title: Fibonacci returns wrong value
description: Returns the n-th Fibonacci number (fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1).
bugExplanation: After n iterations a holds fib(n); b is the next number. Return a.

title: sort() returns None
description: Returns a sorted copy of the numbers.
code:
def sorted_numbers(nums):
    result = nums.sort()
    return result

print(sorted_numbers([3, 1, 2]))
# Run the example above and compare the output with what is expected.
bugExplanation: list.sort() sorts in place and returns None. Use sorted(nums).
hints: Use the function that returns a new list.

title: Wrong zero-division guard
description: Returns a / b, or 0 when b is zero.
bugExplanation: The guard checks for None, not zero, so ZeroDivisionError is still raised. Check b == 0.

title: Unused result of strip
description: Normalizes a user name by trimming whitespace.
bugExplanation: Strings are immutable; strip() returns a new string that is discarded. Assign it: name = name.strip().

title: all instead of any
description: Checks whether a list contains any negative number.
bugExplanation: all() requires every element to be negative. Use any().
hints: Which built-in checks for at least one?
answerOptions: sum(n < 0 for n in nums) == len(nums)

title: Parsing a float string with int
description: Converts the string '3.7' to an integer by truncating.
bugExplanation: int('3.7') raises ValueError because the string is not an integer literal. Parse with float first: int(float(s)).
hints: The string contains a decimal point.

title: Exhausted generator
description: Computes the average of doubled numbers.
code:
def avg_doubled(nums):
    gen = (x * 2 for x in nums)
    total = sum(gen)
    count = len(list(gen))
    return total / count

print(avg_doubled([1, 2, 3]))
bugExplanation: A generator can be consumed only once; after sum(gen) it is empty so count is 0, causing ZeroDivisionError. Build a list instead.
hints: Store the values in a list.

title: Factorial base case misses zero
description: Computes n! recursively.
bugExplanation: fact(0) never hits the base case and recurses forever until RecursionError. Use n <= 1.

title: Shared class attribute
description: Each Basket instance should have its own item list.
code:
class Basket:
    items = []

    def add(self, item):
        self.items.append(item)

a = Basket(); b = Basket()
a.add("x")
print(b.items)  # expected []
bugExplanation: A class attribute is shared by all instances. Create the list in __init__ as self.items = [].

title: Decorator swallows return value
description: A logging decorator should pass through the wrapped function's result.
bugExplanation: wrapper calls func but doesn't return its result so callers get None. Use return func(*args, **kwargs).

title: Quicksort drops duplicates
description: Sorts a list with quicksort keeping duplicates.
bugExplanation: Values equal to the pivot are excluded from both partitions and lost. Use x >= pivot for the right side.
hints: What about values equal to the pivot?

title: Transpose reads wrong cell
description: Transposes a rectangular matrix.
bugExplanation: The source should be matrix[i][j] since i iterates rows and j columns; matrix[j][i] goes out of range for non-square input.

title: Float equality check
description: Checks if two computed floats are equal.
code:
import math

def same(a, b):
    return a == b

x = 0.1 + 0.2
print(same(x, 0.3))  # expected True
bugExplanation: Floating-point rounding makes 0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3. Compare with a tolerance using math.isclose(a, b).

title: Pop on empty stack
description: Checks whether brackets are balanced.
bugExplanation: A closing bracket with an empty stack makes pop() raise IndexError. Check not stack or ... first.
hints: What if the stack is empty?

title: Dedup adds before checking
description: Removes duplicates while preserving order.
bugExplanation: x is added to seen before the membership test, so the test is always False and result stays empty. Add after the check.
hints: Move the add after the if.

title: Sliding window off by one
description: Finds the max sum of any k consecutive numbers.
bugExplanation: The last window start index is len-k, but range stops before it. Use range(len(nums) - k + 1).

title: Unhashable list as cache key
description: Caches results keyed by two arguments.
bugExplanation: Lists are unhashable and can't be dict keys (TypeError). Use a tuple: (a, b).
hints: What can be a dict key?

title: Binary digits in wrong order
description: Converts a positive integer to a binary string.
bugExplanation: Remainders are produced least-significant first so the string is reversed. Join reversed(bits).

title: Flatten appends nested list
description: Flattens arbitrarily nested lists.
bugExplanation: append adds the flattened sublist as one element, leaving nesting. Use result.extend(flatten(x)).

title: Assignment in condition
description: Returns a message saying whether n is zero.
bugExplanation: A single = assigns 0 to n so the condition is always falsy and n is overwritten. Use === for comparison.
hints: Every input gives the same answer.
Look at the operator inside the if.

title: Off-by-one array loop
description: Prints every element of an array.
bugExplanation: Index arr.length is out of range so arr[i] is undefined and .toUpperCase() throws. Use i < arr.length.

title: Arrow function missing return
description: Doubles a number with an arrow function.
bugExplanation: With braces an arrow function needs an explicit return; otherwise it returns undefined. Write return x * 2.

title: Missing null check on nested property
description: Reads a user's city safely.
bugExplanation: address may be undefined causing a TypeError. Use optional chaining: user.address?.city.
hints: TypeError: cannot read properties of undefined.

title: String concatenation instead of addition
description: Adds two numbers that arrive as strings from an input.
bugExplanation: + concatenates strings giving '53'. Convert both values with Number() first.

title: Wrong last-element index
description: Returns the last element of an array.
bugExplanation: arr.length is one past the last index, so the result is undefined. Use arr[arr.length - 1].

title: Reassigning a const
description: Accumulates the total of an array.
bugExplanation: const bindings can't be reassigned so total += n throws TypeError. Declare with let.

title: Wrong logical operator
description: A person may enter if they are 18+ AND have an ID.
bugExplanation: || lets anyone with an ID in even when underage. Both conditions are required, so use &&.

title: Comparing with NaN
description: Detects when a parsed number is invalid.
bugExplanation: NaN is never equal to anything, including itself, so the check is always false. Use Number.isNaN(value).

title: While loop never increments
description: Logs the numbers 0 through 4.
bugExplanation: i is never changed so the condition stays true and the loop never ends. Add i++ inside the loop.

title: Default sort is lexicographic
description: Sorts numbers in ascending order.
bugExplanation: sort() without a comparator compares as strings, giving [1, 10, 100, 9]. Pass (a, b) => a - b.

title: length is not a function
description: Returns the length of a string.
bugExplanation: length is a property, not a method, so calling it throws TypeError. Use str.length.

title: forEach returns undefined
description: Creates a new array with each number doubled.
bugExplanation: forEach always returns undefined. Use map to create a transformed array.
hints: Which method returns a new array?

title: Template literal with wrong quotes
description: Builds a greeting that includes the user's name.
bugExplanation: Template interpolation only works inside backticks. Single quotes print ${name} literally.

title: var in loop closure
description: Logs 0, 1, 2 after a delay.
bugExplanation: var is function-scoped, so all callbacks share one i that ends at 3. Use let for a per-iteration binding.

title: Lost this in callback
description: Increments a counter every 100ms.
bugExplanation: In a regular function callback, this isn't the Timer instance. Use an arrow function to keep the outer this.
hints: What is this inside the callback?

title: Missing await on fetch
description: Loads a user and prints the name.
bugExplanation: fetch returns a Promise; without await res is a Promise with no json method. Use await fetch(...).

title: Comparing arrays with ===
description: Checks whether two arrays have the same contents.
bugExplanation: === on arrays compares references, so different objects are never equal. Compare contents, e.g. JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b).

title: parseInt on decimal strings
description: Converts a price string to a number.
bugExplanation: parseInt stops at the decimal point and returns 19. Use parseFloat.

title: reduce without initial value
description: Sums the price property of cart items.
bugExplanation: Without an initial value, sum starts as the first object, giving '[object Object]7'. Pass 0 as the initial value.
hints: What is sum on the first call?

title: typeof null is object
description: Returns true only for non-null objects.
bugExplanation: typeof null is 'object' in JavaScript, so null passes. Add a null check.
hints: null is treated as an object.

title: Mutating shared nested state
description: Adds an item to a cart without mutating the old state.
bugExplanation: The spread is shallow, so copy.items is the same array as state.items and push mutates both. Create a new array: items: [...state.items, item].

title: splice removes too much
description: Removes one element at index i.
bugExplanation: splice(i) with no count removes everything from i onward. Use splice(i, 1).

title: for...in over array gives strings
description: Adds 1 to each array index.
bugExplanation: for...in yields string keys so '0' + 1 is '01'. Convert with Number(i) + 1.

title: Zero-based month in Date
description: Creates a Date for December 1st, 2024.
bugExplanation: Months are zero-based so 12 rolls into January 2025. Use 11 for December.

title: Debounce timer re-created
description: Debounces a function so only the last call in 200ms runs.
bugExplanation: timer is re-declared on every call so clearTimeout never sees the previous timer. Declare it outside the returned function.
hints: Move it to the outer scope.
answerOptions: declare timer outside the inner function
correctAnswer: declare timer outside the inner function

title: Falsy zero defaulting
description: Uses 3000 as a default port when none is configured.
bugExplanation: || replaces any falsy value, including 0. Use ?? to default only for null or undefined.

title: Async callback in forEach
description: Processes items one by one and logs 'done' afterwards.
bugExplanation: forEach doesn't await async callbacks so 'done' logs immediately. Use for...of with await (or Promise.all with map).

title: Memoize key collision
description: Caches results of an expensive function by arguments.
bugExplanation: Joining with an empty string makes (1,23) and (12,3) both '123'. Use a separator such as ','.
hints: Different calls return the same cached value.

title: Arrow function as prototype method
description: Adds a greet method to Person.
bugExplanation: Arrow functions don't bind their own this so this.name isn't the instance. Use a regular function.

title: Promise chain not returned
description: Fetches a user then their posts, in order.
bugExplanation: The inner promise isn't returned so the next then receives undefined. Use return getPosts(user.id).
hints: The logged posts value is undefined.
What does the first then return?

title: Binary search never moves lo
description: Finds a value in a sorted array.
bugExplanation: lo = mid doesn't shrink the range when lo === mid, creating an infinite loop. Use lo = mid + 1.

title: flat default depth
description: Flattens an array of arbitrary depth.
bugExplanation: flat() flattens only one level by default. Use flat(Infinity).

title: JSON clone loses Dates
description: Deep clones an object that contains a Date.
bugExplanation: JSON serialization turns Dates into strings. Use structuredClone(original).
hints: What does JSON do with Dates?

title: Sort comparator returns boolean
description: Sorts numbers ascending.
bugExplanation: Comparators must return negative, zero or positive numbers; a boolean gives only 0 or 1 and results are inconsistent. Return a - b.

title: Lost this in debounce wrapper
description: Wraps a method so this is preserved.
bugExplanation: Calling fn directly drops the this of the wrapper. Use fn.apply(this, args).
hints: this is undefined in the original.
Who is this in the wrapper?

title: Set of objects does not dedupe
description: Returns the unique users by id.
bugExplanation: A Set compares objects by reference so no duplicates are removed. Dedupe by id instead, e.g. via a Map.

title: Recursive flatten discards concat
description: Flattens nested arrays recursively.
bugExplanation: concat returns a new array and doesn't mutate result, so nested values are lost. Assign: result = result.concat(...).

title: Global regex keeps state
description: Tests several strings against a pattern.
bugExplanation: A regex with the g flag keeps lastIndex between test() calls, so alternate calls fail. Remove the g flag.

title: Floating point money
description: Converts a dollar amount to cents.
bugExplanation: Floating-point multiplication produces values like 1998.9999999999998. Round the result: Math.round(price * 100).

title: Wrong return type annotation
description: Adds two numbers and returns the sum.
bugExplanation: The function returns a number but is annotated as string, causing a type error. Change the return type to number.
hints: The compiler complains about the return.
Compare annotation with the value returned.

title: Loop runs one too far
description: Doubles every element in a numeric array.
bugExplanation: When i equals nums.length the element is undefined, producing NaN. Use i < nums.length.

title: Optional property accessed unsafely
description: Prints a user's profile name if it exists.
bugExplanation: profile is optional and may be undefined, so access can throw. Use user.profile?.nickname ?? user.name.

title: String assigned to number
description: Stores a numeric count.
bugExplanation: A string literal can't be assigned to a number variable. Assign the number 5.

title: Missing return in some code path
description: Returns the absolute value of a number.
bugExplanation: Positive numbers fall through and return undefined. Add return n after the if block.
hints: What if n is not negative?

title: Using = instead of ===
description: Finds whether the status is 'done'.
bugExplanation: = assigns instead of comparing, so the check is always truthy. Use ===.

title: Mutating a readonly property
description: Updates the port of a configuration without mutating it.
bugExplanation: readonly properties cannot be assigned after creation. Create a new object: { ...cfg, port: 8080 }.

title: Index one past the end
description: Gets the final item from a list.
bugExplanation: The last valid index is length - 1. items[items.length] is undefined.

title: Find result used without check
description: Returns the name of the user with a given id.
bugExplanation: find returns undefined when nothing matches, so accessing .name throws. Use ?.name ?? 'unknown'.

title: Union not narrowed
description: Returns the length of a string or the digits of a number.
bugExplanation: number has no length property and the union isn't narrowed. Check typeof x first.

title: Returns wrong element
description: Returns the first element of an array.
bugExplanation: Indexes start at 0. The first element is arr[0].

title: Minimum initialised to zero
description: Finds the smallest number in an array of positive numbers.
bugExplanation: Starting at 0 means no positive number is ever smaller, so 0 is returned. Initialize with Infinity or nums[0].

title: Object.keys returns strings
description: Adds 1 to every numeric key of a record.
bugExplanation: Object.keys returns strings, so '1' + 1 is '11' (and doesn't type-check). Convert with Number(key).

title: Countdown never decrements
description: Collects numbers from n down to 1.
bugExplanation: n is never decremented, so the loop runs forever. Add n-- (or n -= 1) in the loop.

title: Non-null assertion hides null
description: Reads the value of an input element.
bugExplanation: The cast hides that getElementById can return null, causing a runtime TypeError. Add a null check.

title: Missing await on async call
description: Fetches JSON from a URL and returns it.
bugExplanation: fetch returns a Promise<Response>, not a Response. Add await.

title: Async function never returns value
description: Loads a record and returns its value.
bugExplanation: The function computes r.value but never returns it, so the promise resolves to undefined. Use return r.value.

title: Wrong property in discriminated union
description: Computes the area of a shape.
bugExplanation: Inside the 'square' branch the type is the square variant, which has side not radius. Use shape.side ** 2.

title: Spread order overrides user options
description: Merges defaults with user overrides where overrides win.
bugExplanation: Later spreads win, so defaults overwrite the overrides. Reverse the order.

title: sort mutates the original
description: Returns a sorted copy without changing the input.
bugExplanation: Array.sort sorts in place and returns the same array. Copy first: [...items].sort(...).

title: Page default off by one
description: Calculates the offset for a 1-based page number.
bugExplanation: With page = 0 the offset becomes -10. Pages are 1-based so the default should be 1.

title: Generic missing length constraint
description: Returns the longer of two values.
bugExplanation: Type T has no length property. Constrain it: T extends { length: number }.
hints: Property 'length' does not exist on T.

title: Map.get may be undefined
description: Counts occurrences using a Map.
bugExplanation: m.get returns undefined for new keys, producing NaN. Use (m.get(w) ?? 0) + 1.

title: Comparing Dates by reference
description: Checks whether two dates are the same moment.
bugExplanation: === compares object references, not time values. Compare a.getTime() === b.getTime().

title: Callback loses this
description: Registers a class method as a click handler.
bugExplanation: Passing a method detaches it from the instance so this is lost. Define it as an arrow property: increment = () => { ... }.

title: Reduce accumulator type
description: Groups words by length into a record.
bugExplanation: The initial value is an array, but it's used as a keyed record. Use {} typed as Record<number, string[]>.
hints: Keys are added to an array.

title: Optional parameter ordering
description: Greets a person with an optional title.
bugExplanation: A required parameter cannot follow an optional one. Reorder: (name: string, title?: string).
hints: A required parameter cannot follow an optional one.

title: Type guard returns wrong check
description: Narrows unknown values to strings.
bugExplanation: The guard claims x is string but tests for number, so the narrowing is wrong. Use typeof x === 'string'.
hints: Compare the predicate to its claim.

title: forEach with async callbacks
description: Saves each item and then logs completion.
bugExplanation: forEach doesn't wait for promises so 'all saved' logs too early. Use await Promise.all(items.map(save)).

title: Missing case in exhaustive switch
description: Describes each traffic light color.
bugExplanation: The 'yellow' case is missing so the function returns undefined. Add case 'yellow': return 'slow'.

title: Pushing onto readonly array
description: Returns a new list with an extra item.
bugExplanation: readonly arrays have no push, and casting would mutate the input. Return a new array: [...list, item].

title: Reduce typed with wrong initial
description: Sums an object's numeric values.
bugExplanation: Starting from an empty string makes the reduction concatenate, giving '12'. Use 0 as the initial value.

title: Unbound method passed as callback
description: Calls a logger's method through an array map.
bugExplanation: Passing log.format loses this, so this.prefix throws. Use arrow: map((s) => log.format(s)).

title: Tuple swap returns duplicate
description: Swaps the two values of a number pair.
bugExplanation: The function returns a twice, so b is lost and the pair isn't swapped. Return [b, a].

title: Frozen object is shallow
description: Prevents modification of a config including nested data.
bugExplanation: Object.freeze is shallow so nested objects remain mutable. Freeze nested objects too or use deep readonly typing.

title: Promise.all with pushed promises
description: Fetches all users in parallel and returns them in order.
bugExplanation: Awaiting inside the loop runs requests one at a time, not in parallel. Use Promise.all(ids.map(getUser)).

title: Index signature accepts anything
description: Looks up a country code and returns its name.
bugExplanation: Missing keys return undefined at runtime though the type says string, so toUpperCase throws. Handle undefined with ?? or ?.

title: Wrong generic default in merge
description: Merges two arrays of the same type.
bugExplanation: out references the same array as a, so pushing mutates the input. Copy it: const out = [...a].

title: Number compared to string
description: Finds an item by numeric id received from a URL.
bugExplanation: A number is compared to a string with ===, so it never matches. Convert: i.id === Number(idParam).

title: Async map callback returns nothing
description: Fetches several users in parallel and returns their names.
bugExplanation: The async callback doesn't return the promise, so every element resolves to undefined. Use return fetchUser(id).

title: Array loop off-by-one
description: Sums all elements of an int array.
bugExplanation: When i == arr.length an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException is thrown. Use i < arr.length.
hints: An exception is thrown at the end.

title: String compared with ==
description: Checks whether the user name is 'admin'.
bugExplanation: == compares references, not contents, so strings built at runtime won't match. Use equals.

title: Java int division in average
description: Computes the average of two ints as a double.
bugExplanation: sum / count is integer division so 5/2 is 2 before widening to double. Cast one operand to double.

title: Missing return on a path
description: Returns 'positive' or 'non-positive'.
bugExplanation: The else-if branch prints but never returns, so the method doesn't return a value on every path (compile error). Return the string.
hints: What does the second branch do?

title: Possible null dereference
description: Returns the length of a string or 0 if it is null.
bugExplanation: If s is null, s.length() throws NullPointerException. Check for null first.

title: Uninitialized local variable
description: Finds the maximum value in an int array.
bugExplanation: A local variable must be initialized before use. Start with arr[0] or Integer.MIN_VALUE.
hints: Variable might not have been initialized.

title: Assignment inside boolean check
description: Prints a message when the flag is set.
bugExplanation: active = true assigns true and evaluates to true, so the branch always runs. Use if (active).

title: Java while loop never increments
description: Sums numbers 0 to 9.
bugExplanation: i never changes so the loop runs forever. Add i++ inside the loop.

title: Char arithmetic yields int
description: Shifts a letter to the next letter.
bugExplanation: String concatenation appends the number 1 giving 'a1'. Compute (char)(c + 1) first.

title: Last index off by one
description: Returns the last element of an int array.
bugExplanation: a[a.length] is out of bounds. The last element is a[a.length - 1].

title: Factorial overflows int
description: Computes 20! correctly.
bugExplanation: 20! doesn't fit in an int and overflows. Use long.

title: toUpperCase result ignored
description: Converts a name to upper case.
bugExplanation: Strings are immutable; toUpperCase returns a new string that is discarded. Assign it: s = s.toUpperCase().

title: Wrong comparison finding minimum
description: Finds the smallest value in an array.
bugExplanation: Using > tracks the maximum. For the minimum use n < min.

title: Reverse loop skips first char
description: Reverses a string.
bugExplanation: i > 0 stops before index 0, dropping the first character. Use i >= 0.

title: Missing break in day switch
description: Returns the day type for a day number.
bugExplanation: Without break, case 6 falls through into case 7 and ends as 'sunday'. Add break after the case 6 assignment.

title: Concurrent modification
description: Removes all negative numbers from a list.
bugExplanation: Removing while iterating with for-each throws ConcurrentModificationException. Use removeIf or an Iterator.

title: Integer cache comparison
description: Checks whether two boxed numbers are equal.
bugExplanation: == on Integer objects compares references; values over 127 aren't cached. Use a.equals(b).

title: Unboxing null from map
description: Reads a count from a map, defaulting to zero.
bugExplanation: get returns null for a missing key and unboxing null throws NullPointerException. Use getOrDefault.

title: equals overload instead of override
description: Compares two Person objects by name.
bugExplanation: equals(Person) overloads rather than overrides Object.equals(Object), so Object-typed calls use identity. Change the parameter to Object.

title: Static field shared by instances
description: Gives each Item its own id counter.
bugExplanation: id is static so all instances share it and getId returns the latest value. Use an instance field assigned from a static counter.
hints: All items share the same id.

title: Arrays.asList on int array
description: Converts an int array to a List and gets its size.
bugExplanation: Arrays.asList(int[]) creates a List<int[]> with one element. Use Integer[] (or boxed stream).

title: Descending sort comparator reversed
description: Sorts people by age descending.
bugExplanation: x.age() - y.age() sorts ascending. For descending use y.age() - x.age().

title: Array aliasing instead of copy
description: Makes a copy of an array and modifies it.
bugExplanation: Assigning an array copies the reference, not the data. Use Arrays.copyOf.

title: Catch order unreachable
description: Handles a file error and a general error.
bugExplanation: Catching Exception first makes the IOException block unreachable (compile error). Put the more specific catch first.

title: Percentage integer math
description: Computes the percentage of completed tasks.
bugExplanation: done / total is integer division giving 0. Multiply first by 100.0: (done * 100.0) / total.

title: Wrong dimension in 2D loop
description: Prints every cell of a matrix.
bugExplanation: The row loop uses the column count (5) so m[r] goes out of bounds. Use r < m.length.
hints: Index out of bounds on rows.

title: Constructor shadows field
description: Stores a name in a Person.
bugExplanation: name = name assigns the parameter to itself, so the field stays null. Use this.name = name.

title: Missing volatile in double-checked locking
description: Creates a thread-safe lazy singleton.
bugExplanation: Without volatile, other threads may see a partially constructed object because of reordering. Declare the field volatile.
hints: Add a keyword to the field.

title: Non-atomic counter
description: Counts events from many threads.
bugExplanation: count++ is read-modify-write and isn't atomic, so concurrent increments are lost. Use AtomicInteger or synchronized.
hints: Final count is lower than expected.

title: Binary search midpoint overflow
description: Binary search on a very large array.
bugExplanation: lo + hi can overflow int for huge arrays producing a negative index. Use lo + (hi - lo) / 2.

title: Multiplication overflows before widening
description: Computes the product of two ints in a long.
bugExplanation: a * b is computed in int and overflows before being widened. Cast one operand: (long) a * b.

title: Optional get without check
description: Returns the first even number or -1.
bugExplanation: get() throws NoSuchElementException when empty. Use orElse(-1).

title: Remove during iteration with wrong Iterator use
description: Removes empty strings from a list using an Iterator.
bugExplanation: Calling list.remove during iteration invalidates the iterator. Use it.remove().

title: split with regex dot
description: Splits a version string on dots.
bugExplanation: split takes a regex where . matches any character, producing an empty array. Escape it: split("\\.").

title: Memo check inverted
description: Computes Fibonacci with memoization.
bugExplanation: The check is inverted: when the key is missing it calls get (null -> NPE). Remove the negation.

title: Floating point equality
description: Checks whether two sums are equal.
bugExplanation: 0.1 + 0.2 is not exactly 0.3 in binary floating point. Compare within a tolerance.

title: Math.abs of MIN_VALUE
description: Maps a hash code to a bucket index.
bugExplanation: Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) is still negative, so the index may be negative. Use Math.floorMod(h, buckets).

title: wait in if instead of loop
description: A consumer waits until a queue has an item.
bugExplanation: After wait returns the condition might still be false (spurious wakeup or another consumer). Use while.

title: Interval sort uses end
description: Merges overlapping intervals after sorting by start.
bugExplanation: Merging requires sorting by start index a[0], not end a[1].

title: BFS using stack
description: Does a breadth-first traversal.
bugExplanation: add appends to the tail and pollLast takes from the tail, so this is LIFO (DFS order). For BFS take from the head with poll().

title: Vector loop off-by-one
description: Prints all elements of a vector.
bugExplanation: When i == v.size() the access is out of bounds (undefined behavior). Use i < v.size().

title: Uninitialized accumulator
description: Sums the numbers in an array.
bugExplanation: sum is uninitialized so its value is indeterminate. Initialize it to 0.
hints: Look at the declaration of sum.

title: Assignment in if condition
description: Prints when the user is an adult.
bugExplanation: age = 18 assigns and evaluates to true, so the branch always runs. Use age >= 18.

title: Missing return in non-void function
description: Returns the larger of two ints.
bugExplanation: The else-if branch doesn't return a value, which is undefined behavior for a non-void function. Return b.
hints: What does the second branch do?

title: Integer division average
description: Computes the average of two ints as a double.
bugExplanation: sum / count performs integer division yielding 2. Cast one operand to double.

title: Loop never increments
description: Prints numbers 0 to 4.
bugExplanation: i is never incremented so the loop is infinite. Add i++.

title: Vector index at size
description: Returns the last element of a vector.
bugExplanation: v[v.size()] is one past the end. The last element is v[v.size() - 1] (or v.back()).

title: Wrong logical operator for range
description: Checks that a percentage is between 0 and 100.
bugExplanation: With || nearly every number passes. Both bounds must hold, so use &&.

title: sizeof on pointer parameter
description: Computes the number of elements in an array inside a function.
bugExplanation: An array parameter decays to a pointer so sizeof(arr) is the pointer size. Pass the length as a parameter.
answerOptions: int count(int arr[], int n) { return n; }
correctAnswer: int count(int arr[], int n) { return n; }

title: Stray semicolon after loop
description: Prints 'hi' three times.
bugExplanation: The semicolon ends the for statement so the block runs only once after the loop. Remove it.
hints: Look at the end of the for line.

title: Pass by value does not modify
description: Increments the caller's variable.
bugExplanation: The parameter is a copy so the caller's n is unchanged. Take a reference: int& x.

title: Wrong comparison for minimum
description: Finds the smallest element of a vector.
bugExplanation: Using > selects the maximum. For the minimum use x < mn.

title: Adding char* and char
description: Builds a greeting by appending '!'.
bugExplanation: Adding a char to a string literal does pointer arithmetic instead of concatenation. Use std::string and +.

title: int overflow in factorial
description: Computes 15! using an integer.
bugExplanation: 15! exceeds the range of a 32-bit int and overflows. Use long long.

title: Null pointer dereference
description: Prints the value of the first node, if any.
bugExplanation: head may be nullptr and dereferencing it is undefined behavior. Check head != nullptr first.

title: delete instead of delete[]
description: Allocates and frees an int array.
bugExplanation: Memory from new[] must be released with delete[]; using delete is undefined behavior.

title: Erase invalidates iterator
description: Removes all even numbers from a vector.
bugExplanation: erase invalidates the iterator; incrementing it afterwards is undefined. Use it = v.erase(it) and increment only otherwise.

title: Uninitialized pointer write
description: Stores a value through a pointer.
bugExplanation: p isn't initialized so it points to an arbitrary address. Allocate an int or point to an existing one.

title: Unsigned countdown loop
description: Prints a vector in reverse order.
bugExplanation: size_t is unsigned so i >= 0 is always true and i wraps around. Use a signed int index.

title: Switch fall-through
description: Names the day number.
bugExplanation: Without break, case 6 falls through into case 7 and prints both. Add break after case 6.

title: strcpy into a small buffer
description: Copies a word into a buffer.
bugExplanation: 'hello' needs 6 bytes including the null terminator but the buffer holds 5, causing overflow. Use char buf[6].

title: map operator[] inserts
description: Checks whether a key exists in a map.
bugExplanation: operator[] inserts a default value for missing keys, mutating the map and returning false for zero values. Use m.count(k) or find.

title: Returning reference to local
description: Returns a value computed in a function.
bugExplanation: The function returns a reference to a local variable that's destroyed on return. Return by value: int compute().

title: Memory leak with new
description: Allocates a temporary object and uses it.
bugExplanation: The allocated int is never freed, leaking memory every iteration. Add delete p; (or use unique_ptr).

title: Midpoint overflow
description: Binary search over a huge vector.
bugExplanation: lo + hi can overflow int for large arrays. Use lo + (hi - lo) / 2.

title: Comparing doubles with ==
description: Checks a floating-point sum.
bugExplanation: 0.1 + 0.2 isn't exactly 0.3 in floating point. Compare using a tolerance: std::abs(a - b) < 1e-9.

title: Struct member not reset on copy
description: Compares two points for equality.
bugExplanation: The second comparison uses a.x instead of a.y, so equal points compare false. Use a.y == b.y.

title: Use after delete
description: Frees a node and then reads from it.
bugExplanation: Reading from n after delete is undefined behavior. Read the value before deleting.

title: Missing virtual destructor
description: Deletes a derived object through a base pointer.
bugExplanation: Deleting through a base pointer without a virtual destructor is undefined behavior and skips ~Derived. Declare virtual ~Base().

title: Object slicing
description: Stores shapes polymorphically in a vector.
bugExplanation: Storing derived objects by value slices them to Shape so area() returns 0. Store pointers: vector<unique_ptr<Shape>>.
hints: Objects are copied into base type.

title: push_back during range-for
description: Duplicates each element of a vector.
bugExplanation: push_back can reallocate and invalidates the iterators used by the range-for (and the loop never ends). Iterate over a copy.

title: Missing null terminator with strncpy
description: Copies a name into a fixed buffer.
bugExplanation: strncpy doesn't append '\0' when the source is longer than n, so buf isn't terminated. Copy sizeof(buf) - 1 and set the terminator.

title: Data race on counter
description: Increments a shared counter from two threads.
bugExplanation: counter++ from multiple threads is a data race, so increments are lost. Use std::atomic<int>.

title: Shared_ptr cycle leak
description: Models a parent and child that reference each other.
bugExplanation: Two shared_ptrs referencing each other form a cycle, so neither object is freed. Make one link a weak_ptr.

title: Use after move
description: Moves a string into a vector and then prints it.
bugExplanation: After std::move, s is in a valid but unspecified (usually empty) state. Don't use it, or copy instead of move.

title: Uninitialized member in constructor
description: Creates a counter that starts at zero.
bugExplanation: count is never initialized so it has an indeterminate value. Initialize it: int count = 0; or in an initializer list.

title: Invalid strict weak ordering
description: Sorts integers descending with a custom comparator.
bugExplanation: The comparator must be a strict weak ordering; >= returns true for equal elements, which is undefined behavior. Use >.

title: Dangling lambda reference capture
description: Returns a function that adds a stored value.
bugExplanation: The lambda captures n by reference but n dies when makeAdder returns. Capture by value: [=] or [n].

title: Unsigned subtraction wraps
description: Checks whether a is smaller than b.
bugExplanation: Unsigned subtraction wraps to a huge value and is never negative. Compare directly: a < b.

title: string_view of a temporary
description: Prints a substring of a returned string.
bugExplanation: The temporary std::string is destroyed at the end of the statement so sv dangles. Store the string first: std::string s = name().
answerOptions: std::string s = name(); std::string_view sv = s;
correctAnswer: std::string s = name(); std::string_view sv = s;
